title: Proper base change over a finite extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with $A=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$, using [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of noetherian finite-dimensional schemes $X,Y,X',Y'$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Assume $f$ and $f'$ are proper and that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at most some $e\geq0$, as in [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete]. Use the raw rational categories $\Dbc(T,E)=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)[1/\varpi]$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Denote by $Rf_*,Rf'_*,Lg^*,Lg'^*$ the rational extensions, as in [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], of the integral direct images and completed pullbacks in that corollary. The specified rational exchange is the extension of its completed integral exchange. For every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ its component is an isomorphism
$$
 Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',E).
$$

proof.text: The raw rational category has the same objects as the integral category. The spectral absolute value of the integer l is its p-adic norm, which is less than one. The DVR characterization of the maximal ideal and its chosen uniformizer show that l lies in (varpi); hence l annihilates the first coefficient quotient. Use N = l as the positive annihilator in the integral corollary.

Ordinary identity direct image has the normalized isomorphism AdicCoefficientDatum.pushId. The uniform complete predicate is closed under ambient isomorphisms.

proof.text: For each proper map f or f-prime apply the integral corollary to the square with that map on both vertical sides and identity horizontal arrows. Transport membership along the completed identity comparison to obtain preservation by direct image. Pasting the given Cartesian square with the fiber square at y identifies the fiber of f-prime at y with the fiber of f at y composed with g; invariance of topological Krull dimension under isomorphism therefore supplies the same bound e. For g and g-prime apply the corollary to the square with vertical identities and both horizontal arrows equal to that map. The identity fibers are spectra of fields, with discrete topology and dimension at most zero. Transport membership along direct-image identity. All auxiliary corners and annihilator hypotheses are inherited from the given ones.

proof.text: Apply the integral corollary to the original square and the underlying integral object. Its natural isomorphism has ambient component exactly constructibleCompleteExchangeComponent, so that component is invertible. The inclusion of the full constructible complete subcategory reflects isomorphisms; thus the same component is invertible with the membership witnesses just constructed. The defined finiteExtensionRationalExchangeComponent is its image under the actual rationalization functor, and every functor preserves isomorphisms. This proves the specified component is invertible for every raw rational object, including zero and uniformizer-power-torsion objects. No extension of functors or new scalar-linearity theorem is needed for the existing Lean conclusion.
